title: Live Minutes (Fern)
one_liner: Meeting notes that write themselves as you talk: every finished sentence is judged and lands as an action item, decision, question or risk within a fraction of a second.
what_it_does: The page shows one centred column: meeting header (title, four attendees, date, Start button, speed toggles 1x/4x/all-at-once, replay/live-mic switch), a chronological feed of note cards, one line of measured numbers, and a caption strip. In Replay mode a seeded 180-utterance, 12-minute, 4-person product standup plays on a timer. Each utterance, as it "finishes", is sent to the judge with context (speaker, previous 3 utterances, recent decisions, today/sprint-end/launch dates, attendees). The judge answers seven questions at once: kind (action/decision/question/risk/update/chat), assignee, has_deadline, deadline_kind, reverses_earlier_decision, is_blocked, importance. Plain TypeScript then resolves the owner (speaker_themself -> speaker), maps deadline_kind to a real ISO date from the text (src/lib/deadline.ts), gates the owner behind a confidence threshold (<0.6 shows an amber "Who owns this?" chip with per-attendee probabilities the user can click to fix), and strikes through a prior decision when a later one reverses it. Cards show the label, sentence, owner, resolved due date, Blocked flag and a measured end-of-sentence -> on-screen latency. The stats line shows notes count, sentences judged, p50/p95 latency and live/mock source. Live-mic mode uses Chrome Web Speech, segments sentences in code (src/lib/segment.ts), and judges each complete sentence the same way. Keyboard: s start/stop, x reset, r/m replay/mic, 1/4/a speeds.

jev_questions.instructions: Classify `utterance` (said by `speaker` in a product standup) by what a human note-taker would record from it. Use `previous_3_utterances` only for context; judge the utterance itself. Tie-breaks: warns AND assigns follow-up -> action_item; accepting work just assigned to speaker -> action_item; un-agreed proposal -> status_update; bare agreement ('agreed','deal','sounds good') -> chit_chat; handing the floor / agenda logistics -> chit_chat; recap of already-assigned work -> status_update.
options: action_item: Commits a specific person to concrete follow-up work after the meeting ("I'll send the doc", "can you check the logs by Friday?", "Marcus, take the migration", "someone needs to file a ticket").
decision: The group or lead settles what to do or how ("let's go with X", "we're not shipping Y this sprint", "scrap that, keep the old flow"). Not a task for one person, not a mere proposal.
open_question: Raises an unresolved question or asks for information the utterance does not answer.
risk: Warns about a specific thing that could go wrong, slip, break or block the work.
status_update: Reports facts, progress or a proposal without a new commitment or decision.
chit_chat: Greetings, jokes, small talk, acknowledgements, reactions, or logistics of the call itself.
jev_questions.state_shape: {today, current_sprint_ends, launch_date, attendees:[{name,role}], speaker, previous_3_utterances:[{speaker,text}], recent_decisions:[string], utterance}

jev_questions.instructions: If `utterance` assigns, requests, or takes on a task, who is responsible for doing it? If it is not a task, answer unassigned.
options: speaker_themself: The speaker (<name>) commits to doing the task personally: "I'll take that", "I can do it", "let me handle it".
<each other attendee by name>: <Name> (<role>) is asked to do it or accepts it, or the speaker says <First> will do it.
unassigned: A task is raised but nobody specific owns it yet ("someone should...", "we need to..."), or the utterance is not a task at all.
jev_questions.state_shape: same state; criteria built dynamically per speaker from attendees

jev_questions.instructions: Does `utterance` state a due date or time frame for the follow-up work being committed to (e.g. "by Friday", "end of next sprint", "before launch", "tomorrow", "by EOD", "right after this")? criteria.true: A due date, day, or time frame by which the assigned work must be done is stated. criteria.false: No due date for the work: no time reference at all, or the date mentioned is about something else (the launch schedule, an email date, a past event, the meeting itself), or the utterance is not a task.
What kind of due date does `utterance` set for the follow-up work being committed to? Answer none if no deadline is set for the work (dates that are merely discussed as content do not count).
options: specific_date: A named day or date: "Friday", "tomorrow", "tonight", "Monday morning", "the 24th", "October 1st", "today", "right after this", "EOD".
this_week: "this week", "end of week", "EOW", "in the next couple of days".
next_sprint: "next sprint", "end of next sprint", "by sprint end", "before sprint planning".
end_of_quarter: "end of quarter", "EOQ", "by end of Q3", "before the quarter closes".

jev_questions.instructions: Does `utterance` itself decide to reverse, cancel, or replace a decision or plan that was agreed earlier (see `recent_decisions` and `previous_3_utterances`)? criteria.true: The speaker decides to undo or change something previously agreed: "actually, scrap that", "let's not do X after all", "forget Friday, we'll ship Monday". criteria.false: It does not change an earlier decision: confirms the plan, merely proposes or asks about a change, sets a new plan where none existed, or is unrelated.
jev_questions.state_shape: same state; recent_decisions is the last 3 live decisions

jev_questions.instructions: Does the speaker report that work is blocked right now: stuck and unable to proceed until another team, a vendor, an approval, or a dependency delivers? criteria.true: Explicitly stuck now: "the ticket with infra isn't moving", "blocked on the vendor", "the staging API rate-limits us so we can't run it". criteria.false: Not a current blocker: a deadline or ordering, a hypothetical risk, a request, a question, or work simply in progress.
How important is `utterance` for the team to remember after the meeting?
options: Trivial: small talk, a joke, or a detail nobody needs to remember.
Minor: useful context but low stakes; nothing changes if it is forgotten.
Notable: affects the team's plan, a deliverable, or an owner's work this sprint.
Critical: affects the launch date, customers, revenue, compliance, or a hard deadline.
jev_questions.state_shape: same state; score is stored but never rendered in the UI

request_cadence: One Jev request per utterance (7 questions fanned out in that single call). Replay 1x: ~0.25 req/s (180 utterances over 12 min). Replay 4x: ~1 req/s. "All at once": 180 requests in parallel through a concurrency-12 limiter (~20 req/s). Live mic: one request per segmented sentence. Proxy adds 6 s per-attempt timeout and exponential backoff on 429/529/5xx (max 5 attempts).

dm1_mapping.notes: DM1 has no dynamic speaker_themself option; instead the text prefix states the speaker and each attendee label description says 'or <Name> is the speaker and commits personally'. Labels are fixed for the whole meeting so texts batching works. Owner uncertain when probability < 0.6 or label is unassigned; scores gives the per-attendee candidates for the 'Who owns this?' chip. For live mic add the mic speaker name ('You') as a label.

browser_plan: Same Vite/React single-column page, restyled with the milliseconds.ai tokens. Copy transcript.ts, deadline.ts, segment.ts, speech.ts, aggregate.ts, queue.ts, stats.ts, keyword.ts and the five components nearly as-is. Replace server/jev.ts + client.ts with a Cloudflare Worker proxy (demo.milliseconds.ai/api/dm1/*) that holds the bearer key, forwards to https://api.milliseconds.ai/v1/decision-machine-1/{route}, passes x-inference-ms and x-input-tokens back, and returns 429 to the browser untouched. Replace the per-utterance fan-out with a batching scheduler in useMeeting.ts: utterances accumulate in a window; every 500 ms (or when 32 are queued) the window flushes as 5 requests: /classify kind (texts, prefixed with speaker + previous 3), /classify assignee (texts, fixed attendee labels), /classify deadline_kind (texts), /yes-no reverses (texts prefixed with recent decisions), /yes-no is_blocked (texts). A token-bucket limiter caps outbound at 2 req/s, so a full 5-request window takes 2.5 s; at 1x (0.25 utt/s) windows hold 1 utterance and cards land ~0.6-1.5 s after the sentence, at 4x (1 utt/s) windows hold ~3, and "all at once" sends 180 utterances as 6 windows of 30 in ~30 requests over ~15 s. To cut requests, a second option is sequential gating: only kind runs for every window, then assignee + deadline_kind run only on action_item rows and reverses only on decision rows (most windows then cost 2-3 requests). Show the batch size and the measured end-of-sentence -> on-screen p50/p95 honestly in the Pulse line, plus x-inference-ms p50 from headers, so the demo tells the truth about batching latency. On 429: back off with exponential delay (200 ms * 2^n, max 4 s, jitter), keep the window queued, turn the badge amber "rate limited, retrying", and never drop utterances. resolveJudgment maps DM1 responses (label/probability/scores, answer/probability) to the existing Judgment shape so aggregate.ts and NoteCard stay unchanged. Live mic keeps the Web Speech path; each segmented sentence enters the same window. Ship a mock mode using ground truth from transcript.ts as a fallback when the proxy is down.
risks: Headline latency changes: the original promises ~150 ms end-of-sentence -> on-screen with one 7-question request; at 2 req/s and 5 routes per window, the realistic figure is 0.6-2.5 s. The demo copy must be rewritten around that number.

DM1 has no state object; speaker, previous utterances and recent decisions must be packed into the text prefix. Context-heavy judgments (reverses_earlier_decision, assignee via speaker_themself) may lose accuracy versus the Jev 98.9% / 96% baselines; run scripts/eval.ts ported to DM1 before publishing numbers.

The assignee 'speaker_themself' option is dynamic per speaker in Jev; DM1 labels must be fixed for texts batching, so the label descriptions have to cover the 'speaker commits personally' case in prose.
yes-no hints are shared per batch, so each yes-no statement needs its own request; combining reverses and is_blocked as statements[] would lose the hints.

'All at once' mode with 180 utterances is 30 requests minimum; the shared 200 req/min org limit means a handful of concurrent visitors can trigger 429s. The proxy should add a per-IP cap and the UI must degrade gracefully.
Live mic requires Chrome Web Speech; the 'You' speaker must be added to the assignee labels at runtime, and today's date must replace MEETING.today for deadline resolution.
mock-answers.json is Jev-shaped and cannot be reused without conversion; use transcript.ts ground truth as the offline fallback instead.
